solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One's likely to pick things up and set off in large ship

definitions.text: One's likely to pick things up

indicators.note: the clue places the shuffled letters inside the ship, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: an ocean liner is a large passenger ship

indicators.note: set off in the sense of disturbed or knocked askew signals the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets off aboard a big ship, picking things up on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns SET into STE, which 'in' places inside LINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A listener is someone who hears, so picks up sounds and words, a cryptic but fair description.

clue.text: Where food may be left by prison guard after wife leaves

indicators.note: after the wife leaves, her letter is dropped from the guard's word

parts.note: a warder guards inmates in a British prison
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Food abandoned by a prison guard once his wife has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes W from WARDER, giving ARDER, which follows L.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a pantry or cool store room in which food is kept.

clue.text: Removes items of dress that go together

definitions.meaning: verb sense: parts or detaches one thing from another

definitions.text: items of dress that go together
definitions.meaning: noun sense: garments such as skirts and tops sold to be worn in combination

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning detaches and a noun for coordinating clothing pieces.

clue.text: Small amount of water, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a trace, as in 'an ... of truth'
water was one of the four classical ..., with earth, air and fire

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a trace of something and also each of the four ancient elements, water included.

clue.text: Horse-riding competition still on time

parts.note: even and still both intensify, as in 'still better' and 'even better'

explanation.surface: A show-jumping contest is still running to schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a contest in equestrian sport, especially a three-day trial of horse and rider.

clue.text: Exercised with no time to get showered

indicators.note: the exercised word is left with no time letter in it

parts.note: trained means exercised or drilled, as an athlete is

explanation.surface: Someone works out so fast there is no time left to take a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops the first T of TRAINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain falling heavily showers the ground, so rained is a synonym for showered down.

clue.text: Tempt volunteers to turn up with political pamphlet

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the volunteers' letters from bottom to top

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a tract is a short pamphlet on a political or religious issue

explanation.surface: Activists hand out a leaflet to lure volunteers to a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' makes TA into AT.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract someone is to draw or lure them, much as to tempt them.

clue.text: Marine vehicle goes round a loch

indicators.note: the vehicle turns round, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle
L is a common map abbreviation for a loch or lake

explanation.surface: A seaborne vehicle circles a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes round' turns VAN into NAV. A loch is a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine and naval are both adjectives describing things to do with the sea and the navy.

clue.text: Calamity when revolutionary tried to capture crack British troops

indicators.note: the rearranged word captures, so holds, the troops' letters
a revolutionary overturns things, so the letters of tried are thrown into new order

parts.note: the SAS, the Special Air Service, is an elite British army regiment

explanation.surface: A rebel attempts to seize an elite unit, with dreadful results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' makes DITER from TRIED, and 'to capture' puts SAS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden catastrophe, the same as a calamity.

clue.text: Was present at start of Aida before two tenors finished

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Aida is wanted

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor in a choir score, so two give a pair of Ts
ended means finished

explanation.surface: Someone went to the opera's opening before two singers had done.
explanation.walkthrough: Aida is a Verdi opera, fitting the musical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To have attended an occasion is to have been present at it.

clue.text: They should flog politicians?

definitions.meaning: sales reps exist to sell, flog being slang for sell
members of a parliament or congress are elected to speak for voters

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both sales agents and elected members of a legislature, like the US House.

clue.text: Determined adult holding boy? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it, the mark of a container
this reverses the roles stated, so the boy holds the adult rather than the other way round

parts.note: Ernest is a boy's name
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A resolute grown-up keeps hold of a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'adult holding boy': A goes inside ERNEST, not the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes someone serious and resolute, so determined in purpose.

clue.text: Al's been forging permits

indicators.note: forging means fashioning anew, so these letters are hammered into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Al has been faking official permits.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of Al's is fodder, giving ALS.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable something is to allow or make it possible, so enables matches permits as verbs.

clue.text: Sewed top of sweater that ultimately irritated the skin

indicators.note: the top of a word in an across clue is its first letter
ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: something that itched made the skin irritated

explanation.surface: Someone sewed a jumper whose neckline then irritated the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Stitched means joined with needle and thread, which is what sewed means.

clue.text: Hang back the ties with one that's crooked

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of line, so the letters are twisted round

parts.note: A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over a tie that has gone askew.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause or hold back uncertainly, which hang back describes.

clue.text: Lie about British food

indicators.note: one word wrapped about another marks a container

parts.note: a tale is a lie, as in telling tales

explanation.surface: Someone spreads falsehoods concerning British cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Table can mean the food served, as in 'she keeps a good table'.

clue.text: Live with craving for relationship

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
longing means craving

explanation.surface: Living with a yearning for a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging is a sense of affinity or kinship, a relationship with a group or person.

clue.text: Promotes loans

definitions.meaning: verb sense: furthers or moves something forward

explanation.definitionFit: Advances means both furthers a cause and money lent ahead of time.

clue.text: Party in command is Conservative

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of these three words, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: The governing party turns out to be the Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political, and the clue reads as a statement about government, but the letters sit across 'commanD IS COnservative'.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party with dancing to recorded music.

clue.text: Perform musical drama before empty theatre

parts.note: opera is drama set to music

indicators.note: an empty theatre keeps only its first and last letters, the middle removed

explanation.surface: An opera is staged in a theatre with no audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or work, so perform as an intransitive verb.

clue.text: Duly ends broadcast without warning

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A programme ends abruptly, as is proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Suddenly means abruptly, happening with no warning at all.

clue.text: Explanations given by former partner causes one to leave

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: one, as a letter, is made to leave the following word

parts.note: A means one

explanation.surface: An ex-partner's reasons for walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes A from CAUSES, giving CUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Excuses are reasons offered to justify something, so explanations.

clue.text: Picks up some grouse's nests on the way back

indicators.note: the run of letters is read backwards
only some of the letters of these words are used

explanation.surface: Someone collects a few grouse nests while returning.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense something is to detect or perceive it, as one picks up a signal.

clue.text: Old man developed nice tan

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly man has acquired a pleasing suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient is an old person, as in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner.

clue.text: Catholic girl shows style

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A Catholic young woman is very stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Class means elegance or style, as in 'she has real class'.

clue.text: Leave criminal nice cell that's unfinished

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are wrongly handled, signalling an anagram
the cell is unfinished, so its final letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A prisoner is offered parole from a pleasant but incomplete cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's unfinished' cuts CELL to CEL; 'criminal' rearranges NICE plus CEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is formal permission, and leave means permission too.

clue.text: Plump and handsome

definitions.meaning: fat or stout, as a euphemism for a heavy build
generous or sizeable, as in a handsome sum

explanation.definitionFit: Large means stout in build and also generous or substantial in amount.

clue.text: Letters I almost stick inside properties

indicators.note: the following pieces go inside the letters word

parts.note: characters are written letters or symbols

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone nearly glues letters into real estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts STICK to STIC; I plus STIC goes inside CHARACTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Properties in the sense of qualities or traits are distinctive features.

clue.text: Messy for a change? Grabbing servant finally to get order

indicators.note: the shuffled letters grab, so enclose, the next piece
changing the word messy means its letters are shuffled
finally means only the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A messy servant at last tidies the place up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' makes SYSEM from MESSY, and 'Grabbing' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a methodical arrangement, which is what order means here.

clue.text: Reports from wise man in trouble

indicators.note: the wise man is placed inside the trouble word

parts.note: a mess is a predicament or trouble
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Accounts of a learned man getting into difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages are communications sent, which reports also are.
